items.q: What is the scope of a local variable?
items.correct: Accessible only within the function/block where it is declared.
items.random_wrong: Stored on a local computer rather than a server.
items.why: Students confuse 'local' with 'on this computer'. In programming, scope refers to the CODE REGION where the variable name resolves - local variables vanish when the function returns.
The answer examiners want is: Church. “Turing” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: Haskell uses which evaluation strategy by default?
items.why: Correct answer: Lazy. “Strict” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: In what year was Lisp first specified?
items.why: The real figure is 1958. The wrong options cluster deliberately close — anchor the exact number to one concrete fact so it can't drift.
